sources.citation: Leon Festinger, James M. Carlsmith (1959). Cognitive consequences of forced compliance. The Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1959) in The Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: Joel Cooper, Russell H. Fazio (1984). A New Look at Dissonance Theory. Advances in Experimental Social Psychology.
sources.notes: Establishes that induced-compliance attitude change requires perceived free choice and foreseeable aversive consequences.

sources.citation: Daryl J. Bem (1967). Self-perception: An alternative interpretation of cognitive dissonance phenomena. Psychological Review.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (1967) in Psychological Review extending the foundational findings.

sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2013) in La dissonance cognitive extending the foundational findings.

sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (1970) in Journal of Experimental Social Psychology extending the foundational findings.
